clue.text: Pressure on University Blue, drunk after party, to share room

indicators.note: after places the scrambled colour behind the party
in an across clue, on means the pressure letter comes after the university letter

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the word reeling into a new order

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An Oxbridge sportsman, worse for drink after a party, has to bunk in with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns BLUE into UBLE. A Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people doubling up are sharing a room or bed for lack of space.

clue.text: Aneurin greeting African dictator in vacant townhouse

indicators.note: in places the greeting and dictator within the emptied word
vacant means the word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: Someone named Aneurin says hello to an African tyrant in an empty town house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aneurin' looks like a Welsh first name (as in Aneurin Bevan) but is an old name for vitamin B1. 'vacant' leaves T and E of townhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Aneurin is the older chemical name for vitamin B1, a synonym.

clue.text: Discussed division of the church in land surrounded

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: an aisle is a lateral division of a church building

explanation.surface: A church schism is debated in an enclosed territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division of the church' suggests a schism, but it is the physical aisle of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land surrounded by water; this shorter word is a synonym.

clue.text: A cold fish admitting female flaw

parts.note: a chill is a cold

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the female pronoun goes inside the fish

parts.note: the eel is a fish
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: An unfriendly person lets in a woman, revealing a weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold fish' reads as an unfriendly person, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a single fatal weakness, from the Greek hero's vulnerable heel.

clue.text: Playwright set to collect new royalty

indicators.note: to collect means to take in, so the new letter goes inside

parts.note: to set one against another is to pit them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so royalty

explanation.surface: A dramatist is ready to gather fresh royalty payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royalty' suggests an author's payments, which fits the playwright surface, but it is ER, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter was a celebrated English dramatist, an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Liberal friend crosses river

indicators.note: crosses here means spans across, so the friend straddles the river

parts.note: a mate is a friend
the Oder is a river in central Europe

explanation.surface: A politician's friend wades over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal and moderate both describe views that avoid extremes, adjectival synonyms.

clue.text: As alternative, stylish son departs after meal

indicators.note: after puts the departure letter behind the meal

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish
tea is an evening meal in Britain
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A smart son leaves after eating, as a change of plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means as a substitute or alternative, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Living space somewhat limited by Derby?

indicators.note: limited by means bounded on both sides, so the hat surrounds the other phrase

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat
a bit means somewhat

explanation.surface: A restricted living area seems to be what the Derby horse race offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the horse race or the English city, but it is a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or living area of an organism.

clue.text: One to challenge over e-books after pages added

indicators.note: after places the books behind the pages

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
on means added, as in extras tacked on
E stays as written and NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A challenger looks over electronic books after extra pages have been put in.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is a rival, someone who takes you on in a contest.

clue.text: Money problems checked at the outset

indicators.note: checked at the outset means stopped at the start, so the first letter goes

parts.note: trouble means problems

explanation.surface: Financial difficulties were curbed early.
explanation.walkthrough: The ROUBLE is the Russian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency of Russia, an example of money.

clue.text: Number in ocean, returned by nymph, collected by worker

indicators.note: collected by means gathered inside, so the insect surrounds the rest

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

indicators.note: returned means the word for ocean is read backwards

parts.note: sea is an ocean
Thetis was a sea nymph of Greek myth, mother of Achilles

explanation.surface: A figure in the sea is brought back by a nymph and picked up by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure, but it means one who numbs. 'returned' makes AES from SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctor makes patients numb, so is jokingly a numb-er.

clue.text: Addict taken in because relapsed

indicators.note: taken in means contained within the following words, whose letters run across the gap

explanation.surface: An addict is admitted because they slipped back into the habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug addict.

clue.text: Survey ship looks more powerful with this

parts.note: to eye is to survey or look over
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Inspecting an ocean liner makes it appear mightier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' is the noun, a person's appearance or gaze, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up drawn round the eyes gives them a stronger, more striking appearance.

clue.text: Almost fell little man, catching river creature

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the creature goes within the name

parts.note: Ted is a short form of a man's name
the otter lives along rivers

explanation.surface: A small chap stumbled while grabbing an animal from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to stagger and nearly topple over.

clue.text: Glass is raised by detective in Scots town

indicators.note: in places the raised word and detective inside the town

parts.note: Oban is a town on the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A glass is lifted by a detective in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a natural volcanic glass.

clue.text: Be so excited with Star Trek event

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan gets thrilled by a Star Trek happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'event' means a competitive race, as in a swimming gala.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming stroke is also a race at a swimming meet, an event.

clue.text: Bliss in happy house that elevated river devours

indicators.note: devours means swallows, so the river surrounds the other pieces
elevated in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England
up means happy or cheerful

explanation.surface: Joy in a cheerful home that a raised river swallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is intense happiness, a synonym of bliss.

clue.text: Ancient General Staff dismissed from employment, insane!

indicators.note: insane suggests the remaining letters going wildly out of order
dismissed from means removed from the job word

parts.note: staff are the men employed

explanation.surface: A general's staff are sacked from their jobs, which is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy was one of Alexander the Great's generals, later king of Egypt.

clue.text: Soldier to be at forefront of Biblical land

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
to lead is to be at the front

explanation.surface: A soldier hopes to lead the way in a Biblical region.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilead is a mountainous region east of the Jordan in the Bible.

clue.text: Punishment ground?

definitions.meaning: finely powdered, as with ground coffee or sand

explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a money penalty, and fine also means reduced to tiny particles.

clue.text: Very determined that man will become knight with time

parts.note: he is that man
'll is the contracted will
to be is to become
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: He is so determined that he will be knighted in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means recklessly set on achieving something.

clue.text: Gardening in reportedly imperious fashion by river

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: haughty means imperious and a cult is a fashion or craze
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Gardening done in an arrogant manner beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a manner (in the style of), but it is a noun, a craze.
explanation.definitionFit: Horticulture is the science and art of gardening.

clue.text: In lonely place I sold, there lurks mischievous goddess

indicators.note: there lurks means something hides inside the preceding words

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: I sold up in a remote spot, where a troublemaking goddess hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means cut off and remote, describing someone in a lonely place.

clue.text: Having no weak point, excellent fitting holds tons

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written with I for 1

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the tons letter goes inside

parts.note: right means fitting or proper

explanation.surface: A first-rate fitting that holds heavy loads has no weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight argument is watertight, with no flaw to exploit.

clue.text: Learner driver in leather lamped right in the head

indicators.note: in places the learner letter inside the scrambled word
lamped is slang for hit or thumped, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A learner driver in leathers was hit, but remains sound of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamped' rearranges LEATHER as ALTHERE, and the L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all there is mentally alert, sane or sharp.

clue.text: Essentially that's worked to grab attention

indicators.note: to grab means to take hold of, so the attention word goes inside
worked means shaped or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word as written, the 's being a link
ear means attention, as in lend an ear

explanation.surface: Something has been made to catch the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges the letters as ATHT; the surface reads as an attention-seeking display, but 'Essentially' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally, in essence.

clue.text: Offer former partner an amount — five hundred

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ten is an amount, a number
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Offering an ex a sum of five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or hand is to offer it.

clue.text: Top copy with illiterate signature?

parts.note: to ape is to copy
someone unable to write signs with a cross

explanation.surface: A forged signature by someone who cannot write is the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the topmost point or peak.
